extracted.intended_audience: card issuers, industry trade associations, consumer advocates, regulatory compliance professionals, and other stakeholders responding to or implementing CFPB Regulation Z amendments
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and standards for setting and evaluating credit card penalty-fee safe harbors under Regulation Z (§1026.52), including the CFPB's rationale for adopting an $8 late-fee safe harbor for Larger Card Issuers, distinctions for Smaller Card Issuers, and aspects on which the CFPB sought public comment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Late fee safe harbor presumed reasonable and proportional
rubrics_metrics.description: The CFPB preliminarily found that an $8 late fee for the first and subsequent late payments 'better represents a balance of issuer costs, deterrent effects, consumer conduct, as well as the benefits to issuers that result from relying on a safe harbor amount' and therefore is 'presumed to be reasonable and proportional to the late payment violation to which the fee relates.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Supported by analysis of the Y-14 data, consideration of market changes (e.g., automatic payment), and potential beneficial effects on subprime cardholders' repayment behavior. This is the basis for replacing prior safe harbors for Larger Card Issuers with an $8 amount.

rubrics_metrics.name: Charge card special provision (§1026.52(b)(1)(ii)(C))
rubrics_metrics.description: For charge card accounts that require payment of outstanding balances in full at the end of each billing cycle, a card issuer may impose a fee not exceeding 3 percent of the delinquent balance if the issuer has not received the required payment for two or more consecutive billing cycles.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CFPB recognizes this as a form of late fee but did not lower this special provision; the $8 safe harbor applies to other late payments not meeting this charge card description.

rubrics_metrics.name: Elimination of higher safe harbor for subsequent violations (for late fees)
rubrics_metrics.description: The CFPB proposed and adopted that a higher safe harbor dollar amount for penalty fees occurring within the same billing cycle or the next six billing cycles does not apply to late fees for Larger Card Issuers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commentary was amended to clarify that a card issuer cannot impose a late fee in excess of $8 regardless of whether the issuer has imposed a late fee within the six previous billing cycles.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statutory factors to consider when setting late-fee safe harbors
rubrics_metrics.description: Regulatory assessment must consider, at a minimum, issuer costs, deterrent effects, and consumer conduct when determining whether a penalty fee is reasonable and proportional.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CFPB explicitly organized discussion and comment around these statutory factors and used them to justify adopting the $8 safe harbor for Larger Card Issuers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of Y-14 data to assess issuer costs and late-fee revenue
rubrics_metrics.description: CFPB relied on Y-14 data from certain Larger Card Issuers (2013–Sept 2022) showing late fee revenue relative to estimated pre-charge-off collection costs to inform the safe harbor decision.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CFPB used ratios (e.g., late fee income vs. collection costs) and conservative calculations (dividing a prior safe-harbor amount by five) as part of its methodology; commenters contested Y-14 representativeness for smaller issuers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cost-analysis provision (§1026.52(b)(1)(i)) as alternative to safe harbor
rubrics_metrics.description: Card issuers may rely on the cost analysis provisions in §1026.52(b)(1)(i) to set a late fee above the safe harbor if they can justify that amount based on issuer-specific costs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Issuers using cost analysis must be able to demonstrate to the regulator that their determination is consistent with §1026.52(b)(1)(i). CFPB declined to require public disclosure of supporting cost data, citing confidentiality concerns and absence of statutory requirement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consideration of requiring automatic payment or due-date notification as condition of safe harbor
rubrics_metrics.description: CFPB sought comment on whether, as a condition of using the safe harbor for late fees, it may be appropriate to require card issuers to offer automatic payment options (e.g., for the minimum payment amount), provide notification of the payment due date within a certain number of days prior to the due date, or both.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This was posed as a specific question for public comment; commenters' responses could affect final safe-harbor conditions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Whether to eliminate safe harbor provisions altogether
rubrics_metrics.description: CFPB sought comment on whether to eliminate the safe harbor provisions for late fees rather than lowering the safe harbor amounts to $8.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Elimination would force all issuers to rely on individualized cost analysis under §1026.52(b)(1)(i) rather than defaulting to a presumptively reasonable amount.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consideration of lowering safe harbors for other penalty fees
rubrics_metrics.description: CFPB sought comment on whether and why to lower the safe harbor amounts in §1026.52(b)(1)(ii)(A) and (B) for other credit card penalty fees (returned payments, over-the-limit transactions, declined check accesses), including whether to eliminate the higher safe harbor for subsequent violations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requested supporting data on costs of such violations to issuers or arguments for retaining/eliminating safe harbors for those fees.

rubrics_metrics.name: Alternative fee structures (staggered fees, percentage-based thresholds)
rubrics_metrics.description: CFPB sought comment on alternatives such as setting a staggered late fee amount with a cap on the maximum dollar amount (a small dollar amount every certain number of days until a cap) or structuring the safe harbor threshold as a percentage of the minimum payment amount.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requested information on appropriate small-dollar amounts, maximum caps, or percentages and supporting data on effects and reasonableness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendments to commentary for clarity and compliance certainty
rubrics_metrics.description: CFPB proposed revisions to the commentary to §1026.52(b)(1)(ii) for clarity and consistency with lowering the late-fee safe harbor to $8, including revising illustrative examples and explanatory text.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Invited comment on all aspects of the proposed commentary amendments and what additional clarifications may be needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Different treatment for Smaller Card Issuers
rubrics_metrics.description: The final rule does not apply the $8 late-fee safe harbor to Smaller Card Issuers (issuers with fewer than one million open credit card accounts); Smaller Card Issuers retain the safe harbor thresholds in §1026.52(b)(1)(ii)(A)–(C) and CPI annual adjustments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CFPB cited concerns that Y-14 data for larger issuers may not represent smaller issuers' costs; thus different regime retained for Smaller Card Issuers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Annual CPI adjustments and their applicability
rubrics_metrics.description: The annual CPI adjustment provision in §1026.52(b)(1)(ii)(D) will not apply to the $8 safe harbor amount for late fees charged by Larger Card Issuers; however, CPI adjustments will continue to apply for Smaller Card Issuers and for other penalty-fee safe harbors, which were revised to $32 (first) / $43 (subsequent).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CFPB revised other penalty fee safe-harbors pursuant to CPI adjustments and specified non-application to the $8 amount.

rubrics_metrics.name: Safe harbor should not allow fees contrary to statutory standard
rubrics_metrics.description: A discretionary safe harbor should not be set so high that it permits fees that are inconsistent with the statutory standard (i.e., not 'reasonable and proportional'); therefore a safe harbor must be evaluated both for being too low and too high.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CFPB concluded this was an independent reason to repeal prior higher safe-harbors for Larger Card Issuers and replace them with the lower $8 amount.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appropriateness of evidence sources and relevance
rubrics_metrics.description: CFPB noted that some evidence sources (State/local/international approaches, historical fee levels) reflect different policy decisions and are not determinative of whether a safe harbor meets statutory criteria; relevant evidence should relate to issuer costs, deterrence, and consumer conduct.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commenters criticized CFPB for perceived selective use of studies; CFPB emphasized reliance on direct cost data (Y-14) where available.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consideration of issuer cost components in assessing fee reasonableness
rubrics_metrics.description: When evaluating issuer costs, relevant components include direct expenses, attributable expenses, and funding costs (example provided: estimated costs for 60+ day delinquencies: $46.30 total: $33.00 direct, $9.00 attributable, $4.30 funding).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CFPB evaluated commenters' cost submissions and weighed representativeness for different issuer sizes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deterrence: size of fee must deter late payments
rubrics_metrics.description: A factor in determining the fee is whether the amount has a deterrent effect on consumers' likelihood to pay on time; commenters argued $8 may be too low to deter, while CFPB evaluated literature and data regarding deterrence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commenters suggested using proxy comparisons (state return-check penalties, utility late fees, student loan late fees) and cited literature (e.g., Agarwal et al., Grodzicki) on fee-induced behavioral changes such as adoption of autopay.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consumer conduct: accounting for behavior and post-violation risk
rubrics_metrics.description: Consumer conduct focuses on how a consumer's behavior (e.g., prior late payments) affects increased risk to the issuer and whether fee structure appropriately prices augmented risk for repeat late payers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CFPB and commenters discussed whether eliminating higher subsequent-violation safe harbors would inadequately reflect increased risk posed by consumers who pay late multiple times; also considered whether fees encourage inbound/outbound contacts that lead to assistance or payment arrangements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Safety-and-soundness and risk-management considerations
rubrics_metrics.description: Regulatory assessment should consider how fee changes affect issuer risk management, funding costs, pricing (risk-adjusted fees), cash flow, and potential impacts on product availability and pricing for different consumer segments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commenters warned that lost late-fee revenue could force higher interest rates, broader fees, or tightened credit, particularly for institutions subject to rate caps (e.g., credit unions). CFPB considered these arguments in differentiating Smaller vs Larger issuers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of behavioral effects (autopay, inbound calls) in evaluating fee impacts
rubrics_metrics.description: Late fees may prompt consumers to set up automatic payments or to contact issuers, enabling remediation; CFPB considered evidence that initial late fees can reduce future fee incidence and encourage autopay enrollment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commenters provided empirical literature and issuer data showing front-loaded late-fee incidence and subsequent reductions in late fees as consumer behavior changes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Burden of proof for issuers charging more than safe harbor
rubrics_metrics.description: If an issuer charges late fees above the safe harbor, the issuer must be able to demonstrate to the regulator that the fee is justified under §1026.52(b)(1)(i)'s cost analysis provisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Although CFPB declined to require public disclosure of supporting data, issuers must retain and be able to present data to enforcement/regulatory authorities to substantiate higher fees.

rubrics_metrics.name: Invitation to comment on amount and supporting data
rubrics_metrics.description: CFPB solicited public comment on whether to set a different safe harbor amount (and what amount), whether to retain a higher safe harbor, and on what data or information support those positions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CFPB asked for data on costs, deterrence effects, consumer conduct impacts, and alternative safe-harbor designs (staggered fees, percentage-based thresholds) to inform final decisions.
